:::{#thm-conj-product}
#### A complex number times its conjugate

For every complex number $z$,

$$z\,\overline{z} = \abs{z}^2.$$

In particular, $z\,\overline{z}$ is a nonnegative real number.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Write $z = a + b\,i$ with $a, b$ real. Then

$$
\ba
z\,\overline{z}
&= (a + b\,i)(a - b\,i)
&& \text{(@def-complex-conjugate)}
\\
&= a^2 - ab\,i + ab\,i - b^2\,i^2
&& \text{(distribute)}
\\
&= a^2 - b^2\,i^2
&& \text{(cancel } ab\,i \text{)}
\\
&= a^2 + b^2
&& \text{(@def-imaginary-unit)}
\\
&= \abs{z}^2
&& \text{(@def-complex-modulus)}
\ea
$$

:::

::: notes
@axler2024linear [result 4.4, p. 121] lists this identity among the properties of complex numbers.
:::
